Alright. So there is a simple spot at the end of the skip where a link to MTF Alpha-4's hub can be made. Additionally, this skip seems like a great means of investigating film based anomalies, such as SCP-1229. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

MTF Alpha-4 (“Pony Express”) was called to recover SCP-806, SCP-806-1-a, and approximately 50 hours of various types of film.

To this:

MTF Alpha-4 (“Pony Express”) was called to recover SCP-806, SCP-806-1-a, and approximately 50 hours of various types of film.

Changing this:

Complete instances of SCP-806-1 usually retain most memories of their past life, and initially will believe that they are the original individual. All instances save for SCP-806-1-a die of cardiac arrest between 70 and 75 hours after final formation.

To this:

Complete instances of SCP-806-1 usually retain most memories of their past life, and initially will believe that they are the original individual. All instances save for SCP-806-1-a die of cardiac arrest between 70 and 75 hours after final formation. Use of SCP-806 as a means of investigating film based anomalies, including SCP-1229, is pending review.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
So even though I'm sworn to defend the honor of Series I, the idea behind the article does remind me of the reasons why people can sometimes be dismissive of it: it's a bit bare-bones, and seeing that this was a soft rewrite, I don't think you changed much of that core idea. I did like the way you touched up the writing (there's no way you'd get away with saying that something "projects" a living thing nowadays). I neutral-voted because I respected the ending, even though it didn't really impact me the same way it did Aiden-perhaps because I got the "tried to bring someone back and failed" idea, whereas I also agree that Aiden's interpretation is cooler. Had I actually got that vibe on my readthrough, and with some expansion, I might've upvoted.

As a side note, I think it's cool to take the Series I vibe and rewrite it with "modern" site standards, which, as close to objectively as possible, are more stringent now (perhaps because authors themselves have aged significantly). The number of original Series I authors still active and writing is dwindling, so it's a rare opportunity-this is for sure an admirable effort.

item.content:encoded:
For me, this hits a particular note of melancholy at the line about 806-1-a not matching anyone's appearance or history. It's the feeling of seeing an actress you half-remember from a movie you used to love step out from the (literally) silver screen, the feeling of slightly scratched and grainy nostalgia, and not many things manage to tap that particular vein of emotion in me. That in addition to the "I love you." line left me kind of half-stunned as I just sat there pondering who exactly this guy conjured into existence and what motivation he had for it.

Anything that makes me react in that way deserves an upvote.

item.content:encoded:
I like it.

There are a few bits that could be clarified, like what happens if you play the film back multiple times: is multiple copies created?

Also, the length of the film is unrealistic, even for the Foundation. An average 2 hour long movie has 3801.6 meters of film stock (that's about 2.36 miles of film!). (I found this by multiplying the length of one side of 35mm film, which is ~22mm, by 24 fps, divided by 1000 to convert into meters, and then multiplied by 60 for #frames per minute, times 120 for frames per two hours.) For a 289 hour long film, you'd need 549331.2 meters of film (or 341.34 miles of film!) That's just ridiculously large.

Cut it down to 24 hours or so, maybe even 48. That should help with the realism of this. (Yes, I know, I'm a massive nerd. Shush.)

Other than that, just some minor grammar errors that you'll need to fix. Good concept, decent execution, nice premise! Upvoted.
